items.kind: bug (wire contract; S–M) — BREAKING to fix (every service's hash moves once)
items.title: the service CONTRACT HASH does not see a Wire struct's FIELDS: adding a field to, or reordering the fields of, a type an `[rpc]` carries leaves `contract_hash()` unchanged, so under the positional binary codec a redeployed server passes `__contract` and its clients mis-decode
items.body: Repro: `sweeps/order46/papers-46/probes/store/s3_hash_v{1,2,3}.vl`: one service returning `SignalCell<Option<Message>>`; v2 adds `edited: bool` to `Message`, v3 swaps its two fields; all three print `contract_hash=b8fcf645` on 0.43.0. `contract_hash.rs` `render` writes nominal types by declared name and arguments only. `wire.vl`: the binary reader 'advances positionally and ignores [names] — the shared Wire type IS the schema'. Rec (mirrored-store.md Q14): render every Wire struct's and enum's shape (fields in declaration order, resolved types, recursively; variants in order) into the template. The mirrored store (A153) needs it before field-indexed patches can ship. Sizing S–M; compiler (`contract_hash.rs`) + the template slots in rpc.vl.

items.title: `StoreSome::assume()` (what `when_live` hands its body) falls back to the payload AS IT WAS AT THE CALL, not the last value: patch a field through the live variant, end the variant, and the assumed handle reads and wakes with the PRE-patch value
items.body: Repro: `sweeps/order46/papers-46/probes/store/s6_owner_rule_today.vl`: `Store<Option<Message>>` holding `hello`; `assume()`; patch `content` to `edited` (both handles read `edited`); `set(None)`: the assumed `content()` reads `hello` and its observer wakes with `hello`. To spec (`store.vl` doc: 'reads the payload as it was when this was called'), but A153's agreed amendment needs 'hold the LAST value': a row whose message was edited then deleted repaints the pre-edit text for the turn before teardown. Rec: refresh the fallback snapshot on every successful read through the live variant. Sizing S; store.vl + a pin on both ui twins' `when_live`.

items.title: an annotated `let` whose initializer is a BARE closure literal does not adopt the annotation's views, though B465 names it an adopting position: `let typed: \|&str\| void = \|c\| { out = *c; }; typed(&city);` stores the place pair (`Oslo,0`) on JS; the `\|&mut i32\|` twin is refused 'cannot mutate immutable x'
items.discussion: papers-46 (Order 46), closure-type-views.md §1.2 and find 1; root B495
items.body: Repro: `sweeps/order46/papers-46/probes/views/v7b_let_literal_read.vl` (prints `out=Oslo,0`) and `v7_let_literal_adopt.vl` (refused). The same literal handed to a `fun` parameter or a struct field adopts and prints `Oslo` (`v9_read_controls.vl`). Root: B495 (the side table is keyed by the annotation's type id; the binding's `type_id` is not that id when `adopt_closure_parameter_views` reads it), and the mutability check runs before the post-inference pass. Fixed by B495's door (b); pin it either way. Sizing S (pin) / with B495.

items.kind: bug (steer leads to a silent no-op; S)
items.title: a write through a `let` capture of `match &mut place { Some(let p) => p.x = 2 }` is refused with 'declare it `mut`' — and `Some(mut p)` then compiles and DROPS the write (the capture is a copy)
items.body: Repro: `sweeps/order46/papers-46/probes/payload/b2_match_ref_mut.vl` (refused: 'cannot mutate immutable 'p'; declare it `mut` to allow mutation.') and `b1_today.vl` (1) (`Some(mut p)`, `p.x = 2`: `held.x=1`). The steer should say the capture is a copy and how to write the payload (today: `take()`/put back; after B509's door A: a `let` capture under `&mut`, which makes this program legal). Sizing S; diagnostics.

items.kind: UNSOUND (JS: a lost write; native: rustc refusal of an accepted program; M)
items.title: rule 4 does not guard a WRAPPED-VIEW capture: `match first(&mut bag) { Some(let p) => { bag.items = [..]; p.x = 7; } }` compiles and the write lands on the element the list no longer holds
items.body: Repro: `sweeps/order46/papers-46/probes/payload/b9_wrapped_subject_write.vl` with `fun first(bag: &mut Bag): Option<&mut P>`: prints `items[0].x=50` (p.x = 7 lost). The same mutation under a `for e in &mut list` view is refused, 'cannot reassign 'list' while a view into it is live (rule 4 ...)' (`b8_subject_frozen_precedent.vl`). Natively the emitted Rust holds a `&mut bag` borrow across `bag.items = ..`, which rustc refuses (read, not built). Rec: guard the call's `&mut` argument place for the capture's live range, with the same check B509's payload views need. Sizing M; analyzer (rule 4).

items.title: the write-back of a DEAD `mut` match capture deep-clones it on both backends: the Store derive's enum write step `held = E::A(p0)` emits `__replace(held, [0, __clone(p0)])` / `E::A((p0).clone())` though `p0` dies there — half of a through-variant write's 420–470 ms on a 10,000-element payload
items.body: Repro: `sweeps/order46/papers-46/probes/payload/b7_derive_shape_cost.vl`: 2,000 writes of one scalar inside a payload holding a 10,000-element list, through the derive's step shape: 420–470 ms (JS), against 0–1 ms through a `&mut` lend. Emitted: JS `let p0 = __clone($a[1]); f(p0); __replace(held, [ 0, __clone(p0) ])`; native `match (held).clone() { E::A(mut p0) => { f(&mut p0); (*held) = E::A((p0).clone()); } }`. The capture's own clone is B509's (a payload view removes it); the write-back clone of a dead binding is a copy-census miss on its own. Sizing S; the copy-elision pass on both emitters.
